title: Buying a bass clarinet and doubling in Hampton's band
summary: Cobb bought a bass clarinet for $75 from a soldier, borrowed money from Gladys Hampton, and played it behind vocalists in Hampton's band.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: So, anyway, you get on the tenor and you like it, I guess.
Stanley, I haven't been off it since and don't intend to get off of it. That has been my bread and butter over a period of years and I've been in this business now about 47 years this year.
Did you ever have any doubles, I mean, or did you just --
Yes, I doubled. I doubled bass clarinet

in Lionel Hampton's band. I have it here now. I run into a guy going into the Army (IN THE 40's) (unintelligible) and he wanted to get rid of the horn and I didn't know what a bass clarinet was. I'd never seen one before in my life. To be so stupid. And he told me he'd sell it to me for $75.00. I said, "$75.00 for this?" He said, "Yeah." I didn't know the value of a -- I'm ignorant about this. Yeah, he's going in the Army and he could -- he isn't going to come out anymore. He's going across-- you know, he (unintelligible) I guess he did. So I bought it.

I had to go to Gladys Hampton and get the money. I didn't have it. That's Lionel Hampton's wife. But I bought it. I've got it right here now in my closet. I have used it on occasion, but I doubled on it in Hamp's band where Milt Rube Buckner wrote things behind vocalists like Rube Blakeley, maybe Dinah Washington on ballads, maybe Madeline Green, maybe Winnie Brown. I'm talking about mostly on vocal tunes or ballads, and you had all clarinets and a bass clarinet, just like you got all the saxophones and a baritone sax to anchor. I was the anchor man. Okay.
So I learned the principles. You have
different principles in that. And, of course, as you get older -- and I had guys that taught me out of -- of course your registers are different.
And the bottom is one register and when you get up the top, it's just like the saxophone, but it's not like the saxophone on the bottom.
THAT'S WHY A CLARINET'S A HARD INSTRUMENT TO PLAY.
So how did you do it. It's a hard instrument, isn't it?
If you learned clarinet first, you'd be better off to pick up a saxophone after alto, but I didn't learn it first.
